standards.name: ISA Abstract Model
standards.abstract: The ISA Abstract Model is a metadata framework for describing life-science, environmental and biomedical experiments through three core objects: Investigation (project context), Study (unit of research) and Assay (analytical measurements). It captures sample provenance and experimental workflows (often as directed acyclic graphs) and links metadata about sample characteristics, protocols, measurement types, technologies, and data files. The specification is maintained by the ISA community (Susanna‑Assunta Sansone, Philippe Rocca‑Serra, Alejandra Gonzalez‑Beltran, David Johnson, et al., Oxford e-Research Centre) and is implemented in two reference serializations (ISA-Tab and ISA-JSON). It is intended to help software engineers and tool developers enable standardized import/export of experimental metadata to improve reproducibility and reuse.

classification.rationale: The source explicitly lists named properties for core ISA objects (Investigation, Study, Assay, Material/Data/Process nodes, OntologyAnnotation, Ontology) with concrete datatypes in CSV/table form (e.g. 'Identifier - String', 'Submission Date - Representation of a ISO8601 date'). The documentation therefore presents genuine field-level structure (tables) rather than only prose checklists or an ordered DAG, so it should be captured as a MetadataTable.

standards.name: ISA-Tab format
standards.abstract: ISA-Tab describes how to represent experimental metadata for investigations that group one or more studies and assays. Typical research objects are biological investigations (projects) composed of Study units (e.g. chemostat yeast experiments, environmental surveys) and Assays (e.g. microarray, mass spectrometry, sequencing); metadata are encoded as plain-text tab-separated files (Investigation, Study, Assay files) with labeled column headers. The specification (maintained by the ISA-tools community) defines the required sections, the allowed column labels, recommended encodings (UTF-8, ISO8601 dates), and examples; it is used by many tools (ISAcreator, isa4j, converters and viewers) to enable exchange, validation and dispatching of experiment metadata to domain repositories.

classification.rationale: The source material is a formal format specification that defines explicit file-level and column-level structures (Investigation, Study, Assay) and provides concrete header names and datatypes for each column. That is genuine field-level structure (tables of named fields with types), so this is a TABLE.

standards.name: ISA-JSON format
standards.abstract: ISA-JSON is a JSON serialization of the ISA (Investigation/Study/Assay) Abstract Model for representing experimental metadata about biological investigations. The research objects represented are Investigations containing Studies and Assays (sources, samples, materials, processes, data files, protocols, people, publications and ontology references). The format is a set of JSON Schemas (investigation_schema.json, study_schema.json, assay_schema.json, and many sub-schemas) that define typed fields for each entity; documents are encoded in UTF-8 and dates are expected in ISO8601. The specification is maintained as part of the ISA Model and Serialization Specifications (ISA Tools project) and provides machine-readable validation rules and content rules to enable consistent exchange, validation and tooling (conversion, editing, and API support) for ISA-formatted metadata.

classification.rationale: The source material is a set of JSON Schema documents that define concrete named metadata fields with explicit data types (string, array, object, enums, format hints like date-time or uri) for Investigation/Study/Assay and sub-objects. This is field-level structured metadata (a schema), not prose guidance or a simple procedural DAG; therefore it matches the TABLE category.
